info.name: JusPay Checkout PoC (deployed — Stage)
info.description: Same requests as the local collection, pointed at the deployed Adobe I/O Runtime Stage workspace instead of the local dev server (aio app run). Auth uses an OAuth Server-to-Server credential (auto-refreshed via the collection's Pre-request Script) — set the `clientSecret` collection variable before running requests 2-4. See GUIDE.md B-7/B-8 for why a personal `aio auth login` token doesn't work here.

variable.description: Deployed Stage workspace runtime URL — switched back to the original JuspayCheckoutPOC project 2026-09-17 to resolve a technical-account mismatch on the validate-payment webhook (see GUIDE.md B-15). No trailing slash — Adobe I/O Runtime returns 'The requested resource does not exist' on a double slash.
Auto-generated per request; overwritten by the create-session Tests script after a successful call

Passed to JusPay as return_url — must have NO query string (JusPay rejects one that does). Default points at the demo page (../demo/integration-paths-demo.html) served via `npx serve` from the demo/ folder, so paying via this request's paymentLink lands on that page's Step 3, which auto-calls payment-status. Change to any URL you can observe if not running the demo.
Filled in automatically by the create-session request's Tests script

Auto-filled by the collection's Pre-request Script (fetches a fresh Adobe IMS token via the OAuth Server-to-Server credential whenever this is empty or expired). No need to set manually. In the real flow, Commerce supplies its own token automatically — this is testing-only.
Internal — epoch ms when accessToken should be refreshed. Managed by the Pre-request Script, don't edit.

Adobe IMS Org ID for Tekno Point Multimedia India Pvt Ltd Partner Sandbox (org 108480), sent as x-gw-ims-org-id — also required by require-adobe-auth: true actions, alongside the bearer token. Not a secret, safe to keep in this file.
OAuth Server-to-Server credential's Client ID (from Developer Console, JuspayCheckoutPOC project's Stage workspace, switched back 2026-09-17). Not secret by itself.

OAuth Server-to-Server Client Secret — set this yourself in Postman's variable editor (Current value), do NOT put a real value in this file / commit it. Used only by the Pre-request Script to fetch a fresh accessToken.
Scopes for the OAuth Server-to-Server token request — matches the credential's current scopes (updated after adding Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service, see GUIDE.md B-7/B-8). Not secret.

request.description: Calls JusPay's real sandbox POST /orders under the hood, via the deployed action. On success, returns { orderId, paymentLink, status, clientAuthToken }. Open `paymentLink` in a browser to actually pay on JusPay's hosted page before testing validate-payment below — until then the order stays in NEW/CREATED status. This action is require-adobe-auth: false, so no auth headers needed here. Paying will redirect the browser to {{returnUrl}} with order_id/status/signature appended as query params (confirmed empirically — see JUSPAY_INTEGRATION.md section 3).

exec: console.log('Pay here to move this order to CHARGED:', body.body.paymentLink);

request.description: Directly tests the warm-up short-circuit on create-session — require-adobe-auth: false, so no auth headers needed. Should return { warm: true } immediately, without ever calling JusPay or reading stored config. This is what the storefront is meant to fire silently once the customer reaches the payment step, a few seconds before they'd click Pay.

Run this right after create-session, without paying — should return { op: 'exception', message: 'JusPay payment not successful (status: NEW)' } since the order hasn't been charged yet. This confirms we never blindly trust the client. Needs the collection's `clientSecret` variable set (auto-refreshes accessToken via the pre-request script) — a personal `aio auth login` token does NOT satisfy this require-adobe-auth: true gate, see GUIDE.md B-7.

exec: pm.test('status code is 200 (webhook responses are always 200 w/ op field)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 3. validate-payment (after paying via paymentLink — expect success)

request.description: Open request #1's `paymentLink` in a browser first and complete a test payment on JusPay's hosted page, THEN run this. Should return { op: 'success' } once JusPay reports status CHARGED.

Directly tests the warm-up short-circuit added to validate-payment — same require-adobe-auth path as requests #2/#3, so needs a real accessToken (the pre-request script handles this). Should return { op: 'success' } immediately, without ever calling JusPay or reading stored config. This is what payment-status fires automatically after a charge is confirmed (see payment-status/index.js's warmupValidatePayment) — use this request to test the warm-up in isolation, without needing a real charged order first. Check `aio app logs -a payment-method/validate-payment -l 5` for the 'Received warm-up ping' log line to confirm it actually ran, not just that the HTTP call returned 200.

Not exercised by our JusPay-specific logic (it's the scaffold's example filtering unrelated methods like checkmo/cashondelivery/banktransfer), but useful to confirm this require-adobe-auth: true action is reachable at all on the deployed environment.

Our own addition, not part of the base starter kit — this is what the storefront calls directly after JusPay redirects back to `return_url`, to re-verify the real status server-to-server rather than trusting the redirect's own query params. require-adobe-auth: false, same reasoning as create-session, so no auth headers needed. Returns { orderId, status, success }; success is only true once JusPay reports CHARGED.

Directly tests the warm-up short-circuit on payment-status — require-adobe-auth: false, so no auth headers needed. Sent as POST with a JSON body (not the usual GET?orderId=...) since that's exactly how create-session's warmupPaymentStatus() calls it for real — matters because a GET ?warmup=true would arrive as the string "true", not boolean true, and silently fail the === true check. Should return { warm: true } immediately, without ever calling JusPay or reading stored config.
